name: Supinated Barbell Bent-Over Row
nameDa: Foroverbøjet roning med vægtstang og underhåndsgreb
grip: Supinated underhand, around shoulder width; palms face forward away from the thighs at the bottom.
description: Row a barbell toward the abdomen from a hip hinge, using an underhand grip and elbows close to the sides.
setup: Pick up the bar with a controlled hinge, then establish a balanced stance.
Soften the knees and hinge the hips back until the torso is inclined, keeping the back stable.
instructions: Let the bar hang below the knees with the arms extended.
Draw the elbows back to bring the bar toward the lower ribs or upper abdomen.
Keep the torso angle and knee bend steady as the shoulder blades move naturally.
Lower under control to extended arms without dropping the bar or rounding the back.
commonMistakes: Standing up on each pull to move the load.
Jerking the bar or rounding the trunk.

logging.example: A 20 kg bar plus two 15 kg plates: record 50 kg total.
logging.note: Include the bar and both sides' plates; preserve the original load convention in existing logs.

variantNote: Supinated grip with a stable inclined torso. This is a row, not a standing curl; more upright Yates-style setups need their own note.
reviewNotes: Torso angle and grip width may vary; keep the selected setup consistent.
